letter.subject: Concern about cookie and tracking activity after reject choice on smith-nephew.com
letter.body:
Dear Data Protection Officer,

I am writing to raise concerns identified during an automated, passive audit of https://smith-nephew.com on 2026-11-08 04:10 UTC. Using a fresh browser, the audit visited your site, clicked the cookie banner’s reject option (“Deny”), then recorded what was still sent while browsing the site.

The pages visited after rejecting were:
1. https://www.smith-nephew.com/en-GB/patients/treatments
2. https://www.smith-nephew.com/en-gb/allevyn-complete-care-campaign
3. https://educationunlimited.smith-nephew.com/course/view.php?id=2152

Please explain the following points.

1. Our review suggests Facebook advertising tracking started before cookie consent. Facebook advertising requests were recorded before the user had answered the cookie banner. This appears to indicate non-essential advertising technology was active before consent was given.

2. After reject was clicked, Google still received data. We observed 34 requests to doubleclick.net, google.co.uk, google.com and googletagmanager.com after the reject choice. New cookies were also set after reject: IDE, _ga, _ga_NQ6WH7S872, _ga_PYJH0CRNNR, _ga_THV2XCLNPB and _gcl_au.

3. After reject was clicked, Microsoft still received data. We observed 6 requests to clarity.ms and licdn.com after the reject choice.

4. After reject was clicked, Facebook still received data. We observed 2 requests to facebook.net after the reject choice. A new _fbp cookie was set after reject.

5. We reviewed the privacy notice at https://www.smith-nephew.com/en/privacy-notice. We saw no companies named there, but observed Facebook, Google and Microsoft receiving data. The policy may describe recipients by category only, but our review suggests this may not clearly identify who receives personal data.

6. Our review also suggests the privacy notice may be missing the following items: the legal basis for using personal data, who it is shared with, how long it is kept, your rights, how to withdraw consent, and the right to complain to the ICO.

Please:
1. Explain each point above.
2. Confirm which cookies and trackers you consider strictly necessary or otherwise exempt, and why.
3. Stop any non-essential cookies or tracking that operate without consent.
4. Reply within one month.

If this matter is not resolved, it may be raised with the Information Commissioner’s Office.

Yours faithfully,
Joshua Baker
